inputs.label: Sex
inputs.notes: Biological sex. Drives the base column selected for every nutrient. Intersex or transgender users may need to pick the sex matching their current hormonal and physiological profile - consider allowing both to be computed and shown.

inputs.label: Weight
inputs.notes: Body weight in kilograms. Scales energy, water, protein and the nine amino acids. Does NOT scale vitamins or minerals.

inputs.label: Diet type
inputs.notes: Presented as a line spectrum. See diet_spectrum sheet for spectrum positions and the interpolation rule.

inputs.label: Age
inputs.notes: Years. Under 19 returns the AGE_OUT_OF_SCOPE flag - paediatric requirements are a different matrix, not a multiplier.

inputs.label: Sun exposure
inputs.notes: Derived from the latitude of the map location the user picks: abs(latitude) maps to a band on the sun_zones sheet. Affects vitamin D only.

nutrients.notes: Computed from the Schofield weight-only BMR equation times a PAL multiplier; see equations sheet. Not a fixed requirement - it is whatever balances expenditure.

Atrophic gastritis reduces absorption of protein-bound B12. Adults over 50 should meet the RDA from fortified food or a supplement, where B12 is in free form.

The 0.80 g/kg RDA prevents nitrogen loss but does not prevent sarcopenia. PROT-AGE and ESPEN recommend 1.0-1.2 g/kg for healthy adults over 65. Priority 11 so it applies after the activity rule and wins ties.
Values in this dataset are adult DRIs. Under-19s require the paediatric DRI matrix, which is not a multiplier on adult values - per-kg requirements are up to 3x higher during growth.

Endurance training raises iron needs via footstrike haemolysis, sweat and GI losses, and exercise-induced hepcidin.
As above; upper end for high-volume endurance athletes.
Thiamin requirement scales with carbohydrate and energy throughput.
As above.
Riboflavin requirement scales with energy throughput.
As above.
Sweat and urinary magnesium losses rise with heavy training. Evidence is weak; flagged low confidence.
The DRI explicitly states the iron requirement is 1.8x higher for vegetarians, because non-haem iron is poorly absorbed.
Phytate in grains and legumes binds zinc. Up to +50% for high-phytate diets.
Lacto-ovo diets are lower in phytate than fully plant-based ones.
Plant proteins have lower digestibility (DIAAS) and less favourable amino acid patterns; ~+10% total protein compensates.
B12 is absent from all unfortified plant food. A supplement or fortified food is not optional on a vegan diet - this is the single highest-priority warning in the dataset.
Dairy and eggs supply some B12 but often not the full RDA. Monitor status.
No dietary EPA/DHA without fish. Conversion from ALA is inefficient. An algal-oil supplement is the only non-animal preformed source.
Some bodies suggest raising ALA when no preformed EPA/DHA is consumed. Evidence is weak because conversion is rate-limited, not substrate-limited.
Dairy and seafood are the dominant iodine sources in most Western diets. Vegans rely on iodised salt or seaweed, and seaweed content is wildly variable and can exceed the UL.
All three exclude dairy, the dominant calcium source in Western diets. Requirement is unchanged; the sourcing problem is real.
Eggs and liver dominate choline intake. Vegan diets frequently fall below the AI.
Oily fish and egg yolk are the main dietary sources. Vitamin D3 supplements are usually lanolin-derived; lichen-derived D3 and D2 are the vegan options.
Fortified grain is a major folate source in North America. Diets excluding grains lose it, though leafy greens and liver compensate on paleo and carnivore respectively.
Enriched grain is a major thiamin source. Pork, seeds and nuts substitute on paleo/keto.

The 130 g RDA is the amount that avoids reliance on ketones and gluconeogenesis for brain fuel. Under sustained ketoadaptation the brain runs on ketones plus endogenous glucose, so no dietary minimum applies. This is a deliberate override, not a target of zero.
Carbohydrate restriction lowers insulin, which reduces renal sodium reabsorption and causes natriuresis. This is the main driver of early 'keto flu'.
Potassium follows sodium losses. Weak evidence base.
Reported increased magnesium losses on ketogenic diets. Weak evidence base.
Ketogenic diets commonly fall well short of the fibre AI. Low-carbohydrate vegetables, chia, flax and psyllium are the usual remedies.

No plant food means zero fibre by definition. Fibre has an AI rather than an RDA and no deficiency disease is defined, but the colonic-health evidence favours intake. Override set to 0 to reflect the diet, not to endorse it.

The historical scurvy concern. Fresh and organ meat contain small amounts, and some argue low-carbohydrate intake reduces the requirement via less GLUT-mediated competition. The evidence for a lowered requirement is thin - flagged rather than modelled.
Manganese is concentrated in whole grains, nuts and tea. Animal foods are poor sources.
Magnesium is concentrated in plant foods. Animal-only diets are typically low.
Fruit and vegetables dominate potassium intake.

IIFYM is the reference case. Every DRI already assumes a mixed omnivorous Western diet, so no diet multiplier applies. Note the asymmetry: plant-heavy diets get multipliers ABOVE 1, but meat-heavy diets get no multiplier BELOW 1, because the baseline already assumes good bioavailability.
Cutaneous synthesis falls with latitude and stops entirely for part of the year above ~35 degrees ('vitamin D winter'). The RDA assumes minimal sun, so multipliers below 1 credit expected synthesis.

No meaningful cutaneous vitamin D synthesis for 4-6 months of the year at this latitude regardless of time spent outdoors.
The 0.5 multiplier assumes meaningful skin exposure. Indoor workers, heavy sunscreen use, or covering clothing negate it - collect outdoor-hours and skin type to model this properly.

Anyone capable of becoming pregnant is advised to take 400 ug/day of SUPPLEMENTAL folic acid in addition to food folate, because the neural tube closes before most pregnancies are detected. Applied by age band as a proxy for reproductive capacity.
The 18 mg figure assumes average menstrual losses. Heavy menstrual bleeding can raise the true requirement substantially above it.

activity_levels.label: Lightly active
activity_levels.description: Light exercise 1-3 days/week, or a job with some standing and walking.

activity_levels.label: Active
activity_levels.description: Hard exercise 6-7 days/week, or a physically demanding job.

activity_levels.label: Very active

diet_spectrum.label: Vegetarianism
diet_spectrum.description: Lacto-ovo: dairy and eggs, no meat or fish.

diet_spectrum.label: Paleo
diet_spectrum.description: No grains, legumes or dairy. Meat, fish, eggs, vegetables, fruit, nuts.

diet_spectrum.label: IIFYM
diet_spectrum.description: If It Fits Your Macros - unrestricted omnivorous. THIS IS THE BASELINE CASE; every DRI assumes a diet like this.

diet_spectrum.label: Keto

sun_zones.label: Tropical
sun_zones.example_locations: Year-round synthesis possible. Examples: Singapore, Nairobi, Bogota, Darwin, Miami (25N is the boundary).

sun_zones.label: Subtropical
sun_zones.example_locations: Near year-round synthesis. Examples: Cairo, Sydney, Los Angeles, Buenos Aires, Tokyo.

sun_zones.label: Temperate
sun_zones.example_locations: Reference case - matches the RDA's minimal-sun assumption. Examples: Madrid, New York, Rome, Melbourne, Toronto.

sun_zones.label: High latitude
sun_zones.example_locations: Vitamin D winter roughly October to March. Examples: Paris, Vancouver, Montreal, Minneapolis, Milan.

sun_zones.label: Very high latitude
sun_zones.example_locations: Vitamin D winter roughly September to April. Examples: Edinburgh, Stockholm, Moscow, Oslo, Anchorage.

equations.note: BMR = weight_coef * weight_kg + constant. Then energy_kcal = BMR * pal_multiplier. Weight-only form is used because onboarding does not collect height. NOTE: this band is documented as running 5-10% high relative to measured BMR, particularly in non-European populations; it resolves to ~2790 kcal for a low-active 70 kg 25 y male against a published EER of ~2600.
See 18-30 row for the equation form.
See 18-30 row for the equation form.
Validates closely: resolves to 2130 kcal for a low-active 57 kg 29 y female against a published EER of 2130.
See 18-30 row for the equation form.

recommended_extra_inputs.rationale: Without height, energy must come from a weight-only BMR equation (Schofield). Adding height allows Mifflin-St Jeor, which is meaningfully more accurate, especially at the extremes of the height range. This is the single highest-value addition to the onboarding flow.
Fitzpatrick type VI skin needs roughly 3-6x the UV exposure of type II to synthesise the same vitamin D. Without it the sun_zone multiplier is unreliable for a large share of users.

Pregnancy raises iron to 27 mg, folate to 600 ug, iodine to 220 ug and energy by 340-450 kcal. Lactation raises iodine to 290 ug and vitamin A to 1300 ug. Serving unadjusted adult values to a pregnant user is the most consequential error this dataset can make.

Metformin depletes B12; PPIs impair B12, magnesium, calcium and iron; loop and thiazide diuretics deplete potassium, magnesium and thiamin; methotrexate antagonises folate; isoniazid depletes B6. Often the single largest modifier for a given individual.
The DRI adds 35 mg/day of vitamin C for smokers - one of the few modifiers written directly into the reference standard.

Requirements track lean mass, not total mass. At high body fat, per-kg values overshoot; clinical practice uses adjusted body weight. Without this, targets for users above roughly 35% body fat will be too high.
Coeliac disease, Crohn's, and bariatric surgery break the absorption assumption underlying every RDA.
Chronic intake depletes thiamin most acutely - Wernicke encephalopathy is a real risk in heavy drinkers.
The dataset uses age 51 as a proxy. Actual menopause ranges roughly 45-56, so the iron target can be wrong by 10 mg for several years in either direction.
The sun_zone multiplier assumes typical outdoor exposure for the latitude. An indoor worker at any latitude behaves like the temperate or high-latitude case.
